page: Amazon Web Services c6g.medium is a compute-optimized instance powered by a custom AWS Graviton processor. It features a single dedicated physical core and vCPU based on the ARMv8 64-bit architecture (Neoverse-N1) running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the c6g.medium demonstrates moderate single-core performance but sits in the lower tier for multi-core and memory-intensive workloads due to its single-core limitation. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance registers at 1493.38, which is in the average range. However, multi-core metrics, memory bandwidth (such as 19.65 GB/sec read and 9.83 GB/sec write for large blocks), and Geekbench scores fall into the lower decile. Cryptographic operations benefit from hardware-accelerated AES support, though other advanced vector and matrix extensions are absent.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers an entry-level entry point into the ARM64 ecosystem on AWS, providing dedicated CPU resources without the variable performance of burstable instances. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, simple task queue processing, or development and testing environments optimized for ARM architectures.
